sections.title: Order and Degree
sections.content: The 'Order' is the highest derivative present in the equation (e.g., d²y/dx² has order 2). The 'Degree' is the highest power of that highest derivative, but ONLY after the equation is made free from fractional powers and radicals involving derivatives.

sections.title: Formation of Differential Equations
sections.content: To form a differential equation from a family of curves with 'n' independent arbitrary constants, differentiate the equation exactly 'n' times and eliminate all the arbitrary constants.

sections.title: Variable Separable Form
sections.content: If the equation can be written as f(x)dx = g(y)dy, simply integrate both sides: ∫f(x)dx = ∫g(y)dy + C. All 'x' terms must be purely with dx, and 'y' terms with dy.

sections.title: Equations Reducible to Variable Separable
sections.content: Equations of the form dy/dx = f(ax + by + c) cannot be separated directly. Substitute ax + by + c = t, differentiate to get a + b(dy/dx) = dt/dx, and replace dy/dx to make it separable in t and x.

sections.title: Homogeneous Differential Equations
sections.content: A DE is homogeneous if dy/dx = f(x,y) where f(x,y) is a homogeneous function of degree 0. To solve, substitute y = vx (so dy/dx = v + x(dv/dx)). The equation will then reduce to a variable separable form in v and x.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Finding the degree before removing fractional powers from derivatives (e.g., squaring both sides if there's a square root over dy/dx).
2) Forgetting to add the arbitrary constant '+ C' after integration.
3) Incorrectly identifying a non-homogeneous equation as homogeneous because constant terms are ignored.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 1 focuses on identifying the order/degree, forming DEs by eliminating constants, and solving the foundational forms: Variable Separable and Homogeneous equations.

tricks.title: Degree of e^(dy/dx) or sin(dy/dx)
tricks.explanation: If a derivative is trapped inside an exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric function and cannot be isolated, the degree is strictly NOT DEFINED.
tricks.example: d²y/dx² + sin(dy/dx) = 0 → Order = 2, Degree = Not Defined.

tricks.title: Arbitrary Constants Shortcut
tricks.explanation: The order of a differential equation is EXACTLY equal to the number of essential (independent) arbitrary constants in its general solution.
tricks.example: y = A e^(x+B). This simplifies to y = (A e^B) e^x = C e^x. There is only 1 independent constant, so the order is 1.

tricks.title: Quick Variable Separation
tricks.explanation: For equations like f1(x)g1(y)dx + f2(x)g2(y)dy = 0, divide the whole equation by g1(y)*f2(x) to instantly separate the variables.
tricks.example: xy dx + (x+1)y² dy = 0. Divide by (x+1)y → [x/(x+1)]dx + y dy = 0.

tricks.title: Homogeneous Degree Check
tricks.explanation: To quickly check if a function is homogeneous of degree 0, replace x with kx and y with ky. If all 'k's cancel out completely, it is homogeneous.

tricks.title: Orthogonal Trajectories Basics
tricks.explanation: To find the orthogonal trajectory of a family of curves, find its DE, replace dy/dx with (-dx/dy), and solve the new differential equation.
tricks.example: Family of lines y = mx. DE is dy/dx = y/x. Replace: -dx/dy = y/x → x dx + y dy = 0 → Circles x²+y²=C.

tricks.title: Initial Value Problem Shortcut
tricks.explanation: To save algebraic mess, find the value of 'C' the exact moment you finish integrating, before doing any further algebraic simplifications.
tricks.example: ln|y| = x² + C. Put x=0, y=1 immediately to get C=0, instead of changing to y = e^(x²+C).
